truths.truth: The stem census fails loudly in BOTH directions on a mutated tree, printing the offending stem, and such a failure fails `node cadence-core/bin/test.mjs`
truths.evidence: Mutations run in an isolated copy of cadence-core/bin (test.mjs + test-groups.test.mjs + stub stem files) so the working tree was never touched; baseline copy passed 2/2 first. Direction A (extra file on disk): adding planning-zz-probe.test.mjs -> `fail 1`, message 'planning-*.test.mjs on disk that GROUPS.planning does not name: planning-zz-probe - add the stem to the `planning` array in cadence-core/bin/test.mjs...'. Direction B (named stem, no file): removing planning-uat.test.mjs -> `fail 1`, message 'GROUPS.planning entries with no <stem>.test.mjs file in cadence-core/bin/: planning-uat - delete the entry, or restore the file it names'. Both reverted; copy back to pass 2 / fail 0. Wiring to the suite: `node cadence-core/bin/test.mjs --list` lists `test-groups` in `other`; cadence-core/bin/test.mjs's foot is `const r = spawnSync(process.execPath, ['--test', ...files], ...); process.exit(r.status === null ? 1 : r.status)`, so a red arm propagates; the full-suite output contains both test names ('GROUPS.planning is exactly the planning-*.test.mjs files on disk, both directions' and 'the parse reads a real list out of test.mjs, never an empty one'). Vacuity guard is real: cadence-core/bin/test-groups.test.mjs:79-89 asserts NAMED non-empty, four named anchors present, and ON_DISK non-empty. `git status --short` after the probes shows only the pre-existing ` M .planning/FILED.md` and `?? .planning/phases/3/UAT.md`.
